messages:
ci-bot: [ALERT] nightly-bench: small-batch p95 spike detected (+42% vs baseline) for job `nightly-bench-02` (commit abc123d). metric: small-batch-p95. window: 01:00–02:00 UTC. link: https://ci.redwood/alerts/2950012345

devon: saw the alert. quick numbers: baseline p95 ~28ms -> latest ~40ms. p99 ~unchanged. throughput stable.

maria: ugh. thanks for the heads up. anyone see infra changes around that commit window?

ashok: infra rolled `nvidia-driver-525.14` to the bench fleet at 02:14 UTC yesterday. I left a note in infra-change-log.

ops-bot: deployment note: driver rollout completed on bench-nodes group at 02:14 UTC. change-id: infra/driver/2026-03-16-525.14

sara: small-batch test config: dynamic batching ON, max_batch=8, seq_len=512. That flag makes tail sensitive to scheduling preemption.

devon: thanks. the spike is mostly tail latency for single-request pops (small batches). KV/IO times look slightly elevated in traces.

maria: I'm going to try a fast repro on a dev GPU. repro command: ```./scripts/run_small_batch.sh --commit=abc123d --samples=500 --max-batch=8 --seq=512```

devon: also compare with previous commit (abc122f). if you can, run both back-to-back and collect `nsys` short profile: ```nsys profile --output=nb_smallbatch --trace=cuda,osrt -- python bench_small_batch.py --commit=abc123d --samples=200```

maria: grabbing a node now, @ashok can you grant a 3090-dev slot? prefer same driver as bench (525) for parity. :pray:

ashok: granted `bench-dev-3090-03`. driver: 525.14. ssh: ssh dev@bench-dev-3090-03.

devon: when you have a trace, grep for KVCache flush latencies. snippet we saw in previous run: `[2026-03-16T02:21:04Z] KVCache flush time: median=0.12ms, tail=3.1ms` — in the failing run tail -> 8.2ms.

maria: first quick run done. p95 reproduced (~41ms). attaching mini logs: ```[info] batch=1 seq=512 tokens=512 model=redwood-4x
[debug] kvcache_flush=8.1ms cuda_sync=0.9ms step=1
[warn] slow-kv-flush detected``` will upload full trace to gist in a bit.

sara: interesting that cuda_sync isn't big but kvcache flush is. could be lock contention or small memcpy path slowed.

devon: possible regression in our allocator or memcpy path after driver change. @ashok can you diff kernel/driver config between nodes? specifically `nvidia-smi -q` and `dkms status` outputs.

ashok: copying diffs now. quick note: kernel modules same, driver package bumped. no other infra patches in that window.

maria: uploaded nsys trace gist: https://gist.github.com/maria/nb-smallbatch-trace-2950012345. flamegraph attached. see a ~3x increase in `kv_cache::flush()` self-time on device 0.

devon: thanks. action plan: 1) maria to run a second repro with pinned older driver (if possible) or queue a node on pre-rollout snapshot; 2) ashok to try a quick driver rollback on a single bench node and run tests; 3) if rollback fixes it -> open infra revert and hold rollout; 4) if not, deeper profiler (cuprof / device memcpy metrics) and we bisect the runtime change.

maria: queued a repro on a snapshot node (pre-driver). command: `--driver-snapshot=2026-03-15-525.07` queued. will post results in ~20m.

ops-bot: maintenance task created: MAINT-1493 "investigate small-batch p95 spike" assigned to ashok & devon. due: 2026-03-18. link: https://infra/tasks/MAINT-1493

ashok: started rollback on bench-dev-3090-04 (single node) to 525.07. will run quick bench.

maria: pre-driver run initial: p95 = 29ms (baseline). looks like rollback repro'd baseline. posting full logs to the task.

devon: ok that narrows it. sounds like driver 525.14 interacts poorly with our KV flush path. next steps: ashok to confirm across 2 more nodes, as needed open revert PR and hold further rollouts; i'll prepare a minimal reproducer snippet to send to driver vendor if infra prefers to keep driver pinned.

sara: thanks folks. if we end up pinning, let's add a smoke check to nightlies that runs small-batch after driver rollouts to catch this earlier.

maria: noted — will add a quick smoke to nightly-driver-check job and make a tiny PR.

devon: for tracking: i'll open an issue with perf numbers + traces and link MAINT-1493. if anyone finds something else in the meantime ping here. :eyes:
